plugins.name: Vimrc Support
plugins.use: Loads a startup vimrc, so my Vim mappings are identical in Obsidian and in my editor.

plugins.name: Vim Yank Highlight
plugins.use: Flashes the yanked region, must-have

plugins.name: Code Editor Shortcuts
plugins.use: VS Code key bindings (line move, duplicate, multi-cursor) inside the editor

plugins.name: Spacekeys
plugins.use: Leader-key style command sequences, so vault actions are reachable from the keyboard without hotkeys.

plugins.name: Typewriter Mode
plugins.use: Buffer lines below the cursor, so you don't have to work at the edge of your screen.

plugins.name: Quick Latex
plugins.use: Auto-fractions, matrix and align shortcuts, custom shorthands, use immediately

plugins.name: Completr
plugins.use: Autocompletion for LaTeX commands (I disabled it for everything else)

plugins.name: Solve
plugins.use: Inline calculations in plain text: arithmetic, percentages, unit conversion and date math right where I am writing.

plugins.name: Code Emitter
plugins.use: Executes code blocks directly in Document. I use it mainly for syntax verification

plugins.name: VSCode Editor
plugins.use: Convenience plugin. Open arbitrary code files in Vault in a handy editor, not for fullon coding, good for a quick look

plugins.name: Code Language Completer
plugins.use: Autocompletes the language tag on fenced code blocks, so syntax highlighting is never missing because I typed the fence too fast.

plugins.name: Excalidraw
plugins.use: One of the most important elements in My workflow. Quickly draw and Embed handdrawn sketches

plugins.name: Mermaid Tools
plugins.use: Toolbar with common Mermaid elements, making it a smoother experience the few times I use Mermaind.

plugins.name: Obsidian Functionplot
plugins.use: Plots mathematical functions inline.

plugins.name: Mehrmaid
plugins.use: Lets me put real Markdown inside Mermaid nodes, so diagram boxes can hold formatted text and links rather than bare labels.

plugins.name: Diagram Popup
plugins.use: Opens Mermaid / PlantUML / Graphviz diagrams in a zoomable, draggable popup — necessary for wide architecture or pipeline diagrams that do not fit the note width.

plugins.name: Charts View
plugins.use: Renders Ant-Design charts from note data — good for plotting benchmark results or grade and progress data next to the text that explains them.

plugins.name: PDF++
plugins.use: Annotates lecture slides and papers inside Obsidian and links notes back to the exact highlighted passage in the PDF. I usually split-screen the PDF and note.

plugins.name: Media Extended
plugins.use: Built in media player for lecture recordings. Supports timestamped embeds and Screenshots.

plugins.name: Auto Link Title
plugins.use: Pasting a paper, docs page or lecture URL fetches a readable title instead of a naked link.

plugins.name: Paste URL into selection
plugins.use: Select text, paste a URL, get a Markdown link. Just Intuitive behaviour, should be built in.

plugins.name: Linter
plugins.use: Normalises YAML, headings, spacing and math blocks on save, making the vault a bit more normalized.

plugins.name: Smart Typography
plugins.use: Converts quotes, dashes and ellipses to their typographic forms so exported PDFs look properly typeset.

plugins.name: Header Adjuster
plugins.use: Bulk-shifts heading levels up or down

plugins.name: Style Settings
plugins.use: Exposes theme, snippet and plugin CSS variables as real settings, which is how I tune the look of callouts and tables without editing CSS by hand.

plugins.name: List Callouts
plugins.use: Lightweight inline callouts inside lists. See Better Export PDF, only exporter that supports them.

plugins.name: Iconize
plugins.use: Icons on course folders and key notes so I can navigate the vault by shape instead of reading every folder name.

plugins.name: Callout Manager
plugins.use: Lets me define my own callout types (definition, theorem, proof, pitfall) so course notes have a consistent visual grammar.

plugins.name: Hider
plugins.use: Hides specific visual elements. Important for a distraction-free Workspace.

plugins.name: Status Bar Organizer
plugins.use: Reorders and hides status bar items, keeping only the counters I actually watch (edit time, word count) visible.

plugins.name: Hide Sidebars on Window Resize
plugins.use: Collapses sidebars automatically when I shrink the window. This means that notes are always readable, even if I have obsidian only on one side of the screen

plugins.name: Time Things
plugins.use: Clock in the status bar plus tracked editing time per note, giving me real numbers on how long a topic actually took.

plugins.name: Heatmap Calendar
plugins.use: GitHub-style year view fed by Dataview: makes study streaks and gaps in a semester visible at a glance.

plugins.name: Workspaces Plus
plugins.use: Fast switching between saved layouts: One for each Course and usecase

plugins.name: Multiple Notes Outline
plugins.use: Shows the outlines of several notes side by side, which is how I get an overview of a whole course before an exam.

plugins.name: Settings Search
plugins.use: Global search across all settings tabs

plugins.name: Dataview
plugins.use: Queries frontmatter across courses to build dashboards: open exercise sheets, exam dates, which topics I still have not summarised.

plugins.name: Automatic Table Of Contents
plugins.use: Long lecture summaries get a TOC that stays in sync as I keep adding sections during the semester.

plugins.name: Search in Course
plugins.use: My own plugin: scopes float-search to the top-level course folder of the current file, so searching from a Software Engineering note does not return hits from every other module.

getting-things-out.section: Getting things out of the vault
getting-things-out.title: Getting things out of the vault

plugins.name: Advanced Slides
plugins.use: Turns a course note into a slide deck without leaving the vault: Used mainly for tutoring

plugins.name: Better Export PDF
plugins.use: Exports notes as PDFs, produce printable summary sheets for friends. Replaces Obsidian export, because it supports List callouts

plugins.name: Obsidian_to_Anki
plugins.use: Bulk-exports marked passages from my notes into Anki decks, so exam cards are generated from the notes instead of written twice.

plugins.name: Claudian
plugins.use: Embeds Claude Code and other coding agents with the vault as working directory, so an agent can read my notes and PDFs, run shell commands and edit files for me.

plugins.name: Google Calendar
plugins.use: Pulls lecture, lab and deadline events into the vault so planning notes sit next to the actual schedule.

plugins.name: Local REST API with MCP
plugins.use: Exposes the vault over a local REST / MCP endpoint, the bridge that lets external agents and scripts read and write my notes programmatically.

plugins.name: Terminal
plugins.use: A shell inside Obsidian — run a script, a git command or a training job without leaving the note describing it.

plugins.name: Plugin Groups
plugins.use: Enables and disables sets of plugins with one command and delays startup of heavy ones, which keeps this long list from slowing down launch.

plugins.name: Custom Attachment Location
plugins.use: Store embeds near the actual note, not in one big photo wasteland

plugins.name: Update time on edit
plugins.use: Keeps the frontmatter timestamps current automatically, Which is what my Dataview "recently touched" queries depend on.

plugins.name: NLP
plugins.use: Provides NLP primitives (tokenisation, similarity, keyword extraction) that other plugins and my own queries can build on for text analysis over the vault.

plugins.name: BRAT
plugins.use: Installs and updates beta plugins straight from GitHub, which is how the not-yet-released tools in this list get into the vault.
